A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LIVE-KBENCH and KENV. Their complete main texts, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original agent evaluations on 534 kernel bugs, localization and feedback ablations, execution-cost measurements, and LLM-judge validation.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds a Sonnet experiment, temporal-split diagnostics, reproduction-budget analysis, and alternative-judge evaluations.

M1.justification: The KENV environment, agent overlays, run_kernel interface, benchmark pipeline, and patch-evaluation procedures remain unchanged. Gemini 3 Flash still judges equivalence through nine votes with a five-vote threshold; added judge comparisons do not replace this method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 534-bug LIVE-KBENCH-2512 dataset and use the same 79-bug manual-reference set for judge validation. Added models and analyses retain the existing tasks, populations, and temporal partitions.

E2.justification: v3 adds Claude Sonnet 4.5 to the cutoff experiment (Table 2). Appendix D adds Gemini 3 Pro Preview, Claude Opus 4.5, and Gemini 2.5 Pro as alternatives to the existing Gemini 3 Flash judge. The original scaffold and backend comparisons retain their participants.

E3.justification: The added Sonnet experiment specifies temperature 1 and a $5.6 budget. Appendix C introduces evaluation across reproduction budgets of 5–25 attempts on 5,340 patches. Existing splits, metrics, and experimental settings remain unchanged; 25 final-evaluation attempts were already specified in v1.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands validation through temporal-split comparisons of subsystems and patch sizes, reproduction-budget sensitivity, and comparisons of alternative judges. Section 6 also adds qualitative failure analysis, including partial fixes and latent bugs among 52 unresolved cases. These address additional questions about measurement reliability and agent failures beyond the retained ablations.

E5.justification: Appendix C newly discloses five reproduction attempts per runtime feedback call, distinct from the 25 final-evaluation attempts already documented. This is additional repetition information, not evidence of increased runs. Existing averaging and latency-standard-deviation reporting remain unchanged; no confidence intervals or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: The original numerical tables retain their values. New results include Sonnet CRR of 67.85% versus 61.81% and EPR of 13.30% versus 11.29% before/after cutoff (Table 2). Table 11 reports 90, 81, 63, and 51 additional crashes across successive reproduction-budget increments. Table 12 adds alternative-judge accuracies of 86.08–87.34%, below the retained Flash accuracy of 89.87%. Split statistics and failure findings supplement the existing results.

T1.justification: The metric definitions and equivalence criterion remain unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, theorems, proofs, or formal derivations are added; the reproduction-convergence discussion is empirical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same infrastructure contributions, 534-bug release, and headline findings about cutoff performance, patch equivalence, and feedback. Additional evidence supports these claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: Building on v1's existing correctness caveat, v3 explicitly attributes some feedback gains to crash suppression and expands explanations of unsuccessful repairs. It also interprets the temporal subsets as broadly comparable and reproduction increments as converging. These refine the interpretation and limitations of the existing evaluation framework.

D1.justification: v3 adds an explicit artifact-repository link on the first page and documents the five-attempt runtime feedback budget in Appendix C. These improve access information and implementation disclosure; the PDFs do not establish that the underlying runtime setting changed.

R1.justification: Related Work gains an Agents paragraph, references to Live-SWE-agent and the SWE-bench leaderboards, and a fuller explanation of KGYM scheduling. The positioning around live kernel benchmarks and agent-agnostic execution remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds a Discussion section, reorganizes the appendix into dedicated evaluation-parameter and judge-performance sections, and adds conflict-of-interest and funding disclosures. Most existing prose and the main narrative order are retained, with localized explanatory and publication-header edits.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 2, 11, and 12 and replaces Figure 6 with a redesigned dashboard screenshot. Existing tables and figures are relocated or renumbered, including the cost and dataset-distribution plots. The overall two-column design and principal scientific graphics remain stable.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the Sonnet experiment, split diagnostics, reproduction-budget analysis, and judge comparison strengthen the benchmark's empirical support. Failure explanations and artifact-access information improve transparency. The gains remain incremental: split checks cover only selected characteristics, and Appendix C extrapolates to 50 reproduction attempts without testing that budget or quantifying its claimed noise floor.
